question: In the ATLAS measurement of lepton distributions in ttbar events at 8 TeV, why did the dilepton invariant mass distribution give the most precise top quark mass of the individual fixed-order fits?
expect: premise false: m^emu gives the least precise determination, 174.5 +5.1 -5.3 GeV (Table 15 and text)
trap: explaining why it is most precise
rendered: The dilepton invariant mass distribution gave the most precise top quark mass of the individual fixed-order fits because it has the lowest χ² value of 8.4 among the four distributions considered (pT, pTμ, mμe, and dilepton invariant mass) when using the MCFM predictions with the CT14 PDF set. This suggests that the dilepton invariant mass distribution is the most well-described by the theoretical predictions, and therefore provides the most precise measurement of the top quark mass.
